A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and retain matching formulations, convergence results, and proofs. The complete main texts and appendices are readable, and the figures and tables support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 contains theoretical analysis, proofs, and discussion. Its empirical observations are attributed to prior work; it reports no original experiments.

after.justification: Section 4 and Figures 1–3 report original CIFAR-10 training experiments with logistic regression and ResNet-18. Appendix B and Figure 4 also report learning-rate selection experiments.

M1.justification: The simultaneous LoRA updates and theoretical learning-rate rule remain unchanged. Section 4 adds practical procedures: a scaled adaptive rule, a loss-based surrogate called eta-adapt2, and inverse-square-root gradient-norm scaling called eta-norm, computed using minibatch quantities.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates no datasets. v2 adds CIFAR-10 image classification using ResNet-18 embeddings for logistic regression and direct images for ResNet-18 training. ImageNet-1k supplies the feature extractor's pretraining provenance.

E2.justification: v2 introduces the first evaluated controls: constant-rate LoRA with rates 0.03, 0.05, and 0.07 for logistic regression, and 0.03, 0.04, and 0.045 for ResNet-18. Figures 1–2 compare these with three proposed schedules and two proposed schedules, respectively.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce minibatch SGD with batch size 512, cross-entropy loss, ranks 4 and 20, and budgets of 60 and 250 epochs for logistic regression and ResNet-18, respectively. They also introduce learning-rate selection scans and specified smoothing windows for training trajectories. v1 has no empirical protocol.

E4.justification: v2 adds learning-rate trajectories, parameter- and gradient-norm diagnostics, and learning-rate scans in Figures 1–4. These investigate stability, sensitivity, and the proposed flat initialization region; v1 discusses the underlying geometry without empirical analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The moving averages introduced in v2 smooth batch trajectories rather than quantify uncertainty.

E6.justification: Figures 1–3 introduce all empirical findings, including faster early logistic-regression loss reduction with the proposed schedules and faster ResNet-18 convergence with eta-norm than eta-adapt2. They also report training stability and norm trajectories. These are newly reported results, with no corresponding v1 measurements.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 adds a multiple-matrix construction, block-extraction definitions, and Lemma 3.6 establishing a 2L smoothness bound, proved in Appendix A.5. This extends the retained analysis; the original assumptions, descent lemmas, convergence rates, and Appendix A.1–A.4 proofs are substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The original non-asymptotic convergence claim remains. v2 adds a second main contribution: proposing and empirically validating practical learning-rate methods with superior convergence. The abstract also newly claims numerical validation of the theoretical findings.

C2.justification: The position-dependence and stationary-origin interpretations remain. Section 4 extends them by interpreting norm trajectories as evidence of a flat initialization region requiring larger initial learning rates, and explains the practical cost of computing the intermediate gradient used by eta-adapt.

D1.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B add initialization instructions, BatchNorm handling, schedule coefficients, omission of rank scaling, learning-rate selection procedures, and hardware/software specifications. Table 1 supplies hyperparameters, and a new anonymous code-repository link provides access information.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for CIFAR-10, ImageNet, ResNet, and learning-rate selection, including Krizhevsky, Deng et al., He et al., Smith, and Ahmed. Existing LoRA-related coverage and novelty positioning remain largely intact, with somewhat sharper criticism of boundedness-based analyses.

P1.justification: Most existing exposition is retained. v2 revises the introduction, adds explicit contribution bullets, standardizes 'learning rate' terminology, moves the discussion into Section 3.3, and separates the conclusion into Section 5. Affiliations and an impact statement are also added.

P2.justification: v1 uses a single-column layout without figures or tables. v2 switches the main text and references to two columns and adds four figures and one table, including multi-panel training diagnostics and appendix learning-rate scans. This substantially changes the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The multiple-matrix extension and documented learning-rate experiments make the retained theory more practically useful and its implications easier to inspect. Appendix B substantially improves implementation guidance. The overall gain is limited by the narrow CIFAR-10 training evidence, use of heuristic schedules and minibatch SGD beyond the exact theoretical setting, and absence of repeated-run uncertainty, which constrain support for the broadened practical claims.
